text: During this period, the family had to depend on his wife's income and their savings, while he soldiered on in his job search.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Sie Chye came across South Island Aquarium, a company specialising in imports and exports of aquatic plants and ornamental fish.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Although he had to take a pay cut, Sie Chye was keen on the role as he felt the company had good potential and was excited by its expansion plans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The company was also keen to tap on his MNC and management experience.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To better prepare for his role as a Business Manager, Sie Chye was enrolled in the PCP for International Trading Executives.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is a one-year programme to bridge skills gaps in supply chain, trade finance and e-commerce.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: He is now five months into the PCP.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Low Thia Khiang asked about the long-term unemployment situation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In fact, Sie Chye is one of the more than 6,600 individuals previously unemployed for at least six months, which is the definition of long-term unemployed, who found a job through the Adapt and Grow initiative.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is a 25% increase in the number of long-term unemployed placed, compared to 2016.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They account for close to 50% of unemployed jobseekers placed through Adapt and Grow when all the different programmes are combined.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Realistically, not all of the long-term unemployed jobseekers will succeed in the new jobs that we help match them to.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But we are prepared to take some risk, through support programmes, to help them get on their feet.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Otherwise, we risk the pool of long-term unemployed getting bigger and their families falling deeper into difficulties.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, compared to a few years ago, the resident long-term unemployment rate remains slightly elevated.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But it is not at its highest, contrary to what Mr Low Thia Khiang thinks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Nevertheless, we believe there is still much more to do.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Besides helping those already unemployed, like Sie Chye, we are also helping those at risk of displacement.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Vincent had spent a major part of his career performing IT support in the hospitality sector.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, when he saw his company restructuring to cut costs, he thought he should make plans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Although worried that he could not adapt at his age – he is 51 – Vincent also saw an opportunity to learn something new.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Given the strong growth of e-commerce, he saw logistics as a growth sector and signed up for the Attach and Train programme for Logistics Executives.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Unlike the usual PCPs, the Attach and Train programme does not guarantee a job at the start.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is because some sectors or employers are growing but are not yet ready to hire more.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But rather than to wait, the programme helps jobseekers like Vincent build up their curriculum vitae (CV) to be ready for a new career when the opportunities come.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Vincent is currently six months into the Attach and Train programme with ST Logistics.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The company has been suitably impressed by him and is also ready to hire.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Although Vincent’s training attachment will only end this June, ST Logistics has already offered him full-time employment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: He is also a very good example of how the Government can help a mature worker, who has taken proactive steps to overcome his fears, to find a new career in a growth sector.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These mature workers account for about half of all placements under Adapt and Grow.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Last year, MOM announced stepped-up efforts to place local PMETs in five growth sectors with good potential for PMET jobs, namely, infocomm and media, professional services, finance and insurance, wholesale trade and healthcare.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Placements in these five sectors accounted for about 50% of all PMET mismatch placements in the second half of 2017.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Through this effort, we have gained new insights into how we can support the manpower needs of companies that are growing and transforming.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The key is to engage the companies early, before they have firmed up their plans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: By doing so, it is more likely that their existing employees can be a part of the company's future, instead of being just part of the past.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We no longer wait till workers are unemployed or retrenched to reach out to them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Instead, we work with companies ahead of time to put in place redeployment PCPs, such as in Consumer Banking, where existing staff are retrained and redeployed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As the banks transform their frontline services, hundreds of bank tellers and cashiers are adapting to do digital marketing, data analysis and product development.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These staff can avoid painful retrenchment and, at the same time, help their employers meet their new manpower needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In 2018, we expect more placements to come from such redeployment PCPs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our Adapt and Grow efforts are not only targeted at PMETs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A sizeable proportion, about 40%, placed under Adapt and Grow are rank-and-file workers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Similar to PCPs for PMETs, we also have Place and Train programmes for rank-and-file workers to reskill to take on new roles.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have also piloted the Work Trial scheme in 2016.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This scheme is targeted at jobseekers who are job-ready but are not sure about the specific jobs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It could also be that the jobseeker and prospective employers are unsure about each other.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Through Work Trial, they have up to three months to assess each other, with Government bearing the cost.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Sahfari left his previous job as a sales manager in an IT solutions company as he felt the environment was not quite suited for him.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, he was still keen on a sales position as he enjoys interacting with people.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: He found out that Crosstrack was hiring a sales manager.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In case you are wondering, Crosstrack is a startup which provides an online marketplace to allow customers to source for the most suitable courier for their delivery jobs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Unlike his previous sales jobs which were focused on direct sales, Crosstrack's requirement of a sales manager includes operations management and liaising with delivery drivers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: He thought to himself, could he cope with the additional workload and does a tech startup offer sufficient job security?

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Therefore, he decided to sign up for Work Trial before committing on a permanent basis.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Through the Work Trial, Muhammad had the opportunity to try out a new job in an unfamiliar environment, in a startup.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Not only did he enjoy the dynamic nature of a startup, he also picked up new IT skills.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Crosstrack saw that he had the right aptitude and attitude and employed him on a permanent basis when the Work Trial ended.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So far, the Adapt and Grow initiative has been able to provide the appropriate interventions for jobseekers at different stages, as highlighted by Mr Patrick Tay.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, we are always looking for better ways to scale up, enhance existing programmes or introduce new ones which will help jobseekers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This year, we will make three enhancements to Adapt and Grow.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Second, we will also do more for our rank-and-file workers, a suggestion raised by Assoc Prof Faishal Ibrahim.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In particular, to further encourage employers to hire long-term unemployed rank-and-file workers, we will raise the salary support for such workers under the Place-and-Train programme from 70% to 90% of monthly salary.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will also increase the maximum monthly payout to employers from $2,000 to $3,000.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Third, there is scope to enhance the upward mobility of lower- to middle-income workers by helping them take up better jobs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Part of this is done through efforts under LEDS to uplift and transform jobs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But the other part is helping workers to access such jobs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Work Trial has proven useful in plugging information gaps.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Without Work Trial, Sahfari would likely have missed out on a good career opportunity in a growth sector and Crosstrack would have missed out on a good hire.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Desmond Choo will be glad to know that we will expand the current scope of Work Trial to provide workers with more opportunities to try out better jobs, specifically better paid jobs, and help companies which need more manpower to assess jobseekers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Chairman, the Adapt and Grow initiative is a viable way to help Singaporeans have better employment outcomes even as our economy restructures.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will continue to improve on the scheme designs and intensify our outreach to enable more Singaporeans to be matched to good jobs and careers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Chairman, if you allow, I would like to wrap up this section in Mandarin.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Chairman, the Adapt and Grow initiative had reaped significant results in the past few years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Through this initiative, we managed to help more than 25,000 Singaporeans find jobs last year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is 20% more than the year before.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In particular, there was an increase in the placement of mature workers, long-term unemployed and PMETs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will maintain the current momentum, enhance support and increase our scope of coverage through various programmes to ensure that Singaporeans are able to take up new jobs and adapt to the demands of this new era, even if they have to make a switch in their careers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Chairman, besides helping Singaporeans find good jobs, MOM also set up a tripartite work group (TWG) last year to study the challenges faced by SEPs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Last month, TWG submitted a set of useful proposals, which have been accepted by the Government.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will work with our tripartite partners to implement these proposals progressively in the next two years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Thirdly, we will work with interested SEP associations to develop occupation-specific frameworks to ensure that SEPs are equipped with relevant skills.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Fourthly, we will launch a new insurance product to mitigate SEPs' loss of income during prolonged injury or illness.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Fifthly, we will study how to promote adoption of the abovementioned insurance for higher-risk occupations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Sixthly, the Government will pilot the "contribute-as-you-earn" model to help SEPs save in their MediSave accounts, and study how other corporate service buyers could also adopt this model.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I will elaborate on the implementation timeline for these proposals in English.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, for the last decade, SEPs have constituted 8% to 10% of our resident workforce.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At the COS debate last year, Minister Lim Swee Say highlighted the possible increase in the number of SEPs, given the emergence of the gig economy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This was the impetus for setting up TWG to look into the concerns of SEPs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Before I give the Government's response to the TWG's recommendations, let me first provide an update of the SEP landscape, which will also address questions and concerns raised by Mr Thomas Chua, Ms Jessica Tan and Mr Kok Heng Leun.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This growth took place at the same time as regular employment among residents also went up.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: All the increase in the number of SEPs came from those who did self-employed work as their main jobs, rather than as secondary sources of income.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Such SEPs are referred to as "primary SEPs" because they depend on self-employment primarily for their livelihoods.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Primary SEPs are also the group we are most interested in.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Primary SEPs now constitute 8.4% of our resident workforce, still well within the range of 8% to 10% observed over the last decade.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: What do we know about the age and education profiles of primary SEPs, and have they changed in 2017?

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: By age, more than half of the primary SEPs are 50 and above; less than 10% are below 30.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The age distribution in 2017 remains largely the same as 2016.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, the share of primary SEPs with tertiary qualifications rose from 37% to 40%, in tandem with the rise in education profile among the local workforce.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But it is still much less than the 55% tertiary-educated in the local workforce.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The most recent survey also showed a notable increase in the number of primary SEPs who said they preferred regular employment over self-employment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This group rose from 19% in 2016 to 23% in 2017.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In other words, about one in five primary SEPs prefer to be in a regular job.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, they tend to be older and have lower educational qualifications.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are very keen to help them and Mr Ang Hin Kee asked how.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: First, is to improve the SEPs' awareness of job matching schemes available and encourage them to come forward to the career centres run by WSG and NTUC-e2i.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our existing schemes, as well as the new Career Trial programme that I spoke about, can also help.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Certainly, we should help career counsellors and coaches become more aware of these efforts so that they can provide the right advice.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But these efforts will need such SEPs to become active jobseekers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At present, more than 80% of them say they have not been looking for a regular job actively, even though they prefer it over self-employment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For the vast majority of SEPs who continue to prefer self-employment as a career, we should also address their concerns and provide them with support.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To recap, TWG noted in its report that although the SEPs were very diverse, there were four common challenges they faced.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: First, payment-related disputes; second, loss of income due to prolonged illness or injury; third, lack of CPF savings for healthcare and retirement; and fourth, lack of occupation-specific competency frameworks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Thomas Chua, Ms Jessica Tan and Mr Ang Hin Kee asked about MOM's response.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are grateful to the TWG members who include Mr Ang, for your well-considered and balanced recommendations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Some observers have suggested mandating written contracts for all SEPs to minimise payment disputes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The TWG considered this but finds it impractical.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is because buyers of SEPs' services include micro-SMEs and even individual households, such as for private home tuition.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This was developed with tripartite partners in line with the TWG's recommendations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It is an agreed benchmark which SEPs should encourage buyers to adopt.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: SEPs will be able to identify and contract with progressive service buyers who adopt the standard.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Buyers who adopt the standard need to discuss and agree clearly, with the SEPs, terms of engagement, such as the range of services to be delivered, project timelines and milestones, payment schedules.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These will have to be set out in writing.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The standard is a good start to make clear the working arrangements between businesses and SEPs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Over time, the standard will help shape contracting norms and entrench best practices.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But even with written agreements, disputes could potentially still arise.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For SEPs with sector agencies, we encourage them to continue to approach their sector agencies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These sector agencies would be in a better position to help resolve disputes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For instance, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) facilitates mediation of disputes between taxi operators and taxi drivers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: LTA is best suited for this role because, apart from being familiar with issues in the industry, it has convening power as the regulator of both taxi operators and taxi drivers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For other SEPs, from September last year, TADM started piloting voluntary mediation when they have payment disputes with businesses.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Additionally, the TWG recommended that a prolonged medical leave (PML) insurance product be developed to mitigate the SEPs' loss of income during prolonged injury or illness.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Today, some SEPs buy additional riders on top of their private insurance plans to provide for this.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, there is a lack of an affordable standalone PML insurance product today.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This means that SEPs have no alternative if they do not wish to buy the main insurance product.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Observers and SEPs have also asked if service buyers should be made to buy insurance for SEPs, just as businesses buy work injury insurance for their employees.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, unlike a regular employee, most SEPs contract with multiple service buyers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It will not be possible to determine precisely how much coverage each service buyer should provide for the SEP.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will, therefore, take a practical approach of making the insurance product available for SEPs to purchase for their own protection.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I am encouraged that NTUC Income is keen to develop a PML insurance product that will fulfil the TWG's recommendations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Other insurance companies may also step forward to offer such insurance.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They can be found in numerous occupations, many of which have low-risk of injury, such as real estate agents.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We, therefore, agree with TWG that the purchase of PML insurance should largely be kept voluntary.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: That said, we want to encourage widespread adoption of insurance by SEPs in some higher-risk occupations, as they are most in need of such protection.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Making insurance coverage the norm for SEPs in these occupations would make clear to the buyers of their services that the insurance costs would be priced into their fees.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As a start, we have identified two occupational groups in which to promote PML insurance coverage.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The first group is sports coaches and instructors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Collectively, Ministry of Education (MOE) schools are major buyers of their services.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: SEP coaches and instructors may then price the cost of PML insurance coverage into their bids for MOE's work or projects.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The individual buyers of their services are really the commuters, and there are many.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But there are significant intermediaries like the taxi operators and matching platforms like Grab and Uber.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Together, sport coaches, taxi and private hire car drivers comprise about 30% of all SEPs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In consultation with relevant stakeholders, MOM will also work closely with MOE and LTA on the way forward to promote PML insurance coverage as a norm, starting with these two occupational groups.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Government also accepts the TWG's recommendation to help SEPs save more regularly for their healthcare and retirement needs through a "contribute-as-you-earn" (CAYE) model.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: CPF is the cornerstone of our social security system.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: CPF schemes are not limited to regular employees.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: SEPs can also make use of CPF to save for their healthcare and retirement needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Currently, SEPs are already required to contribute to their MediSave accounts on an annual basis.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They can additionally make voluntary CPF contributions to build up their retirement savings.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Even though MediSave contributions are mandatory today, about one in four SEPs have not been keeping up with their MediSave contributions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Well, this is because SEPs are given up to 12 months from the time income is assessed to make their MediSave contributions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A key challenge is that they may not set aside enough cash on a regular basis.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, when the time comes to make that lump-sum contribution to their MediSave accounts, they find it difficult to do so.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Without sufficient MediSave contributions, these SEPs may not be able to pay for out-of-pocket healthcare expenses or keep up with their MediShield Life premiums.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They will face a longer-term risk of not being able to pay for their healthcare in old age.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This means that a MediSave contribution is required as and when a service fee is earned, similar to employees today who pay CPF when they receive their monthly salaries.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The service buyer or intermediary who contracts with the SEP will deduct and transmit the MediSave contribution to the SEP's MediSave account whenever they pay the SEP.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There is no change to the SEP's obligation to make the MediSave contribution and, for the time being, neither will we require SEPs to contribute to their Special Account to build up their retirement savings.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: While this is an important issue, this matter should be reviewed only after we have effectively addressed the problem of SEPs defaulting on their MediSave contributions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Chen Show Mao offered several suggestions to nudge SEPs to make voluntary contributions beyond MediSave.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We thank him for his suggestions and will study their feasibility.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Realistically, CAYE can only work for SEPs who contract with corporate service buyers or get work through certain significant intermediaries.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The individual hirer of a private home tutor, for example, will not be in a position to help the SEP make his MediSave contribution.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Intermediaries who work with SEPs, such as Grab and Caregiver Asia, have indicated their support for CAYE.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But CAYE will not be straightforward to roll out.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will have to work through implementation issues, such as the correct amount of MediSave contributions to deduct in each transaction.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Government, as a service buyer, will take the lead to implement CAYE.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In the meantime, we welcome companies to continue their voluntary MediSave contributions for their SEPs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The final recommendation by the TWG is for the tripartite partners to support SEP associations in developing occupation-specific competency frameworks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our tripartite partners are committed to doing so.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These Skills Frameworks provide key information on sector, career pathways, occupations/job roles, and the skills required for these occupations/job roles.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They also list the training programmes that individuals or employers can tap on.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The information in these Skills Frameworks will be relevant to both employees as well as SEPs in those sectors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Freelancers and Self-Employed Unit (U FSE) in the Labour Movement is also working with many groups, such as the sports coaches, to develop a training and accreditation scheme.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There are SEP associations that have proactively helped their SEPs to learn new skills.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, NTA, under the leadership of Mr Ang Hin Kee, saw that foundational digital skills, as well as familiarity with digital applications, such as Parking.sg and mobile payment apps, would benefit its members in their day-to-day work.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They also knew the course schedule had to cater to taxi drivers' unique work schedules.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: NTA worked closely with one of the SkillsFuture Singapore's (SSG's) appointed training providers and SSG to customise the SkillsFuture for Digital Workplace programme for NTA members.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: SSG also provides course fee subsidies for the programme to keep the cost affordable for the drivers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If I understand correctly, they pay about $50 for each course.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: SEP associations can strengthen support to help their members make their SEP careers more sustainable.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Government and the tripartite partners are keen to work with more SEP associations on this front.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Chairman, let me summarise the Government's response to the TWG’s seven recommendations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The recommendation to introduce CAYE for other service buyers will require further study.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Government will focus on selected occupations where there are significant intermediaries or where there are large corporate service buyers we can work with.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are confident that the TWG recommendations will help address the main common challenges that SEPs face.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: And we will continue to monitor the SEP landscape to stay on top of the changing trends.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Chairman, as we look to support SEPs better, we are also committed to making our workplaces progressive for all, including for our women.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Over the last three years, it averaged 72%, higher than the 69% average in the previous three years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In terms of full-time employment, we are ranked sixth, compared to 35 Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) countries.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: With more women in the workforce, has workplace harassment become a bigger problem?

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Together with the tripartite partners, we have taken a multi-pronged approach towards protecting people against workplace harassment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Employees who experience workplace harassment should seek help promptly, including for attacks on employees in cyberspace, as raised by Ms Thanaletchimi.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They can report such incidents to MOM, as well as to TAFEP, which Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin suggested.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They can also seek civil remedies directly through the Courts or report serious cases to the Police.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Between 2013 and 2017, an average of about 20 Police reports were filed annually involving sexual harassment or insults of modesty occurring at the workplace.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They were thoroughly investigated and the offenders taken to task.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Some employees prefer to resolve the matter privately without involving the authorities but would rather report the matter to their employers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Legislating mandatory reporting by employers, as suggested by Ms Thanaletchimi, will close off this avenue for such employees and discourage them from raising the matter with anyone.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Instead, the tripartite partners introduced the Tripartite Advisory on Managing Workplace Harassment in 2015 to remind our employers of their obligations to prevent and manage workplace harassment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They should also inform the employees of the avenues where they can seek help.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Last year, we also launched the Tripartite Standard on Grievance Handling which covers workplace harassment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Three hundred and twenty employers adopted the standard, covering about 260,000 employees.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A mediation body called for by Ms Thanaletchimi already exists as TADM can also mediate harassment cases.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: What about gender pay gap which Dr Intan Mokhtar was concerned about?

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh cited a study by ValuePenguin.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I think he did so during the debate on the Budget, and the study said that gender pay gap "has remained at around 18% to 19%" from 2006 to 2016.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Unfortunately, the study did not make an apple-to-apple comparison as it included both full-time and part-time employed residents.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: More women than men worked part-time to meet their family and caregiving responsibilities and naturally earned less.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: MOM's Comprehensive Labour Force Survey allows us to look at only full-time employed residents and compare salaries of men and women in similar occupational groups.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But this is a significant improvement from 20% 10 years ago.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There was also broad-based improvement across most occupational groups.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The remaining pay gap can be attributed to the fact that women are more likely to exit the workforce or have intermittent patterns of work for reasons, such as childcare and sometimes caring for the elderly.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If and when they return to the workforce, as a result, they also have to catch up with their male counterparts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The same reason probably explains why more men than women achieve retirement adequacy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In 2017, 66% of active male members and 53% of active female members turning 55 met their CPF BRS.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, 66% for the active male CPF members, and 53% for the active female CPF members.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong will be pleased to know that the gap is closing.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In 2007, the median retirement savings for women at age 55 were about 60% of median balances at age 55 for men.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: By 2017, 10 years on, this ratio has improved to 74%.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: And we expect the gap to further narrow over time.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To address Assoc Prof Daniel Goh's concern about the gender difference in CPF LIFE payouts, the best way is really to enable the women to remain in the workforce, so that they continue to advance in their careers and build up retirement savings.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This was the key thrust of my speech last night at an event organised by the Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCCI) to celebrate International Women’s Day.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This enhancement comes on top of the Tripartite Standard on FWAs launched last year which now covers some 250,000 employees.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Tripartite Standard on Unpaid Leave for Unexpected Care Needs which I launched a few days ago during the COS debate on the Prime Minister's Office (PMO); and, thirdly, the very significant expansion of preschool places which the Government is fully committed to.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These measures that I have highlighted will help the current and future cohorts of younger women remain in the workforce and improve their retirement adequacy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For the older cohorts of women who still did not manage to save enough for retirement, we have introduced a number of measures to help.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In 2016, we made it easier for members to transfer CPF savings to their spouses’ account by lowering the minimum threshold they must meet, from the Full Retirement Sum to the Basic Retirement Sum.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: From October 2018, we will also make it easier for children to transfer CPF savings to their parents and grandparents.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Chairman, overall, with our tripartite efforts, we have made progress in helping Singapore women to better manage their family responsibilities and work aspirations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There is certainly more to be done, and we will continue to strengthen our efforts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Chairman, beyond helping our workers gain access to good jobs and have good employment outcomes, we also want to help them have better retirement adequacy for better peace of mind in old age.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our CPF system serves Singaporeans well in supporting our three basic needs, namely, housing, healthcare and retirement.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Today, six in 10 active CPF members turning age 55 have at least the BRS in their Retirement Accounts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: By 2020, we expect this proportion to increase to 70% and even more over time.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To help CPF members save more for their retirement, we stepped up efforts to encourage members to top-up their own or their loved ones’ CPF accounts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Forty percent of these members who received cash top-ups, CPF transfers or both, had less than BRS.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In other words, these top-ups and transfers were very useful to them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have also enhanced WIS and introduced Silver Support to provide additional retirement support to lower-income Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They constitute about 30% of the population of seniors aged 65 and above.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I am pleased to share with Members that about two-thirds of the Silver Support recipients are women.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I think this shows very clearly that we are not averse to helping those who need more help and that, of course, includes women, especially those of the previous generation who did not have as much of a runway to build up their retirement savings.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh asked if the payouts can be the same, regardless of flat types.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Although all Silver Support recipients are already means-tested, the degree of family support they enjoy is not the same.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The purpose of Silver Support is to top-up and to help those who perhaps do not have as strong family support and also because they accumulated too little during their productive years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, housing type is not a perfect proxy for family support, but it is an uncomplicated indicator.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Singaporeans with exceptional circumstances can appeal to be eligible for Silver Support or to receive higher payouts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Since the scheme started in July 2016, about 10,000 appeals had been received.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: About half were approved because of the appellant's changed circumstances.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is why it is also not so meaningful to look only at those who drop out from Silver Support because there are also those who qualify.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There are those who did not qualify in the past but then subsequently qualify.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, there are people who used to get it but no longer get it because the assessment is updated regularly and they no longer meet the eligibility criteria.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But there are also people who did not meet the criteria in the past, but then subsequently were able to.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The important thing is that about 30% of seniors above the age of 65 continue to receive Silver Support.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Leon Perera asked about giving CPF members flexibility with their mandatory CPF contributions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But I should emphasise that the primary purpose of CPF is to save for our retirement.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Today, while the CPF system is enabling more Singaporeans to have adequate savings in retirement, there are still groups that we want to help build up retirement adequacy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, as pointed out by Members like Dr Intan Mokhtar and Mr Zainal Sapari, low-wage workers and older workers continue to need help.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Besides the schemes that I have described earlier, we have also tightened rules on CPF withdrawals for everyone, precisely to ensure that retirement savings continue to be steadily built up and are not depleted.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For those who have built up substantial CPF savings, we are helping them grow those savings in better ways, which I will talk about later.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It will, therefore, be incongruent with our current focus to start loosening up, whether in terms of the rules on withdrawal or contributions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Let us stay focused on the task at hand, safeguard and grow our CPF savings so that all Singaporeans can have better peace of mind in retirement, for as long as they live.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Chairman, Mr Zainal Sapari expressed concerns that some CPF members who invest through the CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) might not fully understand the risks and costs involved.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, their painstakingly built-up retirement savings may be lost.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Currently, there are two ways for members to grow their CPF savings.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For those who have no appetite for risk, they can earn risk-free interest on their CPF savings.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Those who have an appetite for risk may choose to invest their monies through CPFIS.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, a member who is willing to take risk may not have the knowledge to invest.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Based on a poll commissioned on behalf of the CPF Advisory Panel in 2015, more than half of the CPFIS investors considered themselves to have "limited" investment knowledge but it did not prevent them from taking those investments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: CPF members should exercise caution when investing their CPF savings.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have been studying the feasibility of a third option for this group of members and the scheme is called the Lifetime Retirement Investment Scheme (LRIS).

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This LRIS is targeted at CPF members who have an appetite for risk but neither the knowledge nor time to invest.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We want to take advantage of the longer time horizon available to CPF members to earn better upside investment gains.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Yet, the product should also provide some assurance against downside risks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Members can well imagine that such a scheme is not easy to design and will require further study.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In the meantime, we will make three enhancements to better cater CPFIS to members with an appetite for risk and have both the knowledge and time to invest.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: First, we will introduce a self-awareness questionnaire (SAQ) that will be available to all CPF members.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This questionnaire will provide feedback to the member on his level of basic financial knowledge and remind him of the different options available to him to grow his CPF savings, such as CPF interest rates or the upcoming LRIS.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But regardless of the feedback, members can still decide whether or not to invest through the CPFIS.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The questionnaire will be part of the process of opening a CPFIS account from 1 October this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Members who already have a CPFIS account are not required to take the questionnaire but are strongly encouraged to do so.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Currently, financial advisors can receive a sales charge of up to 3% of the transacted amount when members use their CPF to purchase unit trusts and investment-linked insurance policies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This sales charge has an unintended consequence that is detrimental to CPF members' interests.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It encourages financial advisors to sell products to earn more commissions which causes the members to "churn" their investments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our target group of CPFIS members will generally not need to rely heavily on financial advisors to decide which investment products to purchase.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They can already directly buy unit trusts on online platforms, such as FundSupermart, Navigator and POEMS for zero sales charge.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Therefore, the sales charge adds another layer of cost that reduces the member’s investment returns.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: By removing the sales charge, financial advisors no longer have an incentive to push products.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This also reduces the cost of investing for CPFIS members and will better align the investment behaviour to members who have time and knowledge.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The third enhancement is to reduce the maximum wrap fees charged for CPFIS investments such that wrap fees cover only the cost to maintain wrap accounts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For Members' information, currently, some CPF members set up a wrap account on investment platforms.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Financial advisors can charge an annual wrap fee of up to 1% of the amount of funds that they manage in the wrap accounts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The wrap fee covers advisory services and the costs to maintain the wrap account.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are not opposed to wrap accounts as they are generally considered to bring convenience to investors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is similar to the fees charged by online investment platforms in the cash market.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will review the cap on wrap fees from time to time as the investment landscape evolves.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are mindful that these enhancements may affect the financial advisory industry which will no longer be able to impose the sales charge on new CPFIS investments and will have to charge only lower wrap fees on wrap accounts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, we do not expect this impact to be too substantial.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: (In Mandarin):   Chairman, we will enhance the CPFIS to further protect the interests of CPF members.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Through self-awareness, CPF members can better understand which option is most suitable if they want to achieve the best returns from their CPF savings.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For members who do not have enough time or who are unfamiliar with investments, leaving their CPF savings in their accounts to earn risk-free interest may be the most ideal option.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our SEPs and CPF members will also enjoy better protection.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: MOM will continue to improve our schemes and programmes to ensure that we have an inclusive workforce and progressive workplaces.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have our work cut out for us and we look forward to Members' support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Chairman, the Minister and Second Minister for Manpower spoke about the need to transform and grow, and to adapt and grow.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: In line with these efforts, I will focus on how we will better support older and low-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: I will also talk about promoting an inclusive, safe and healthy workplace for our workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The employment outcomes of our older workers have improved over the years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Our older worker employment rate is higher than countries, such as Australia, Korea, the US and UK.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: In fact, compared to the 35 OECD countries, Singapore would be ranked among the top 10.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The unemployment rate of older residents has also remained low at below 3% over the last five years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This is comparable to the overall unemployment rate.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This means that the vast majority of older residents in the labour force who want to find a job can find a job.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: And for those who need assistance to find a job, we will continue to help them through the Adapt and Grow initiative.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Last year, we took further steps to enhance the employability of our older workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We are heartened to see that both employers and workers have embraced the re-employment concept and our older workers have benefited.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Since re-employment was introduced in 2012, over 98% of private sector local employees who wished to continue working were offered re-employment at age 62.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Of those who were re-employed in the same job, 98% did not experience any cut in their basic wages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: While results are encouraging, we hope to do even more and better.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Hence, one key priority is to ensure that both jobs and workplaces become more conducive for our older workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We agree with Dr Intan Mokhtar and Mr Chen Show Mao on the importance of job redesign.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: It can transform work processes for older workers, which Ms Jessica Tan has also brought up.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Since WorkPro's enhancement, WSG, NTUC-e2i and the Singapore National Employers' Federation (SNEF) have funded more than 650 companies, benefiting more than 10,000 older workers aged 50 and older.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Through working with companies, we learnt that job redesign not only makes older workers' existing jobs easier, safer and smarter, it also creates new jobs and opportunities for them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: One example is Mdm Toh Kim Pong, a 69-year-old employee at Goodwood Park Hotel.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: In the past, two younger employees were needed to transport linen to the laundromat.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: To do this, they have to push trolleys manually, carrying up to 100 kilogrammes (kg) of linen, up a steep slope and across an open-air carpark.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Because of her age, this was a task that Mdm Toh could not do.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The hotel then decided to tap on WorkPro to introduce motorised trolleys and train older workers like Mdm Toh to operate them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: As a result, Mdm Toh is now able to take on a new task previously too strenuous for her.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This has also led to a wage increase for her.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Given the success story of Goodwood Park Hotel, I encourage more companies to make their jobs age-friendly through the WorkPro Job Redesign Grant, which is part of LEDS mentioned by the Second Minister earlier.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This will also support the growing pool of older Singaporean workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong and Miss Cheryl Chan have asked about age-friendly workplace practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Patrick Tay and Ms Tin Pei Ling also surfaced this issue of ageism.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The tripartite partners share these concerns, too, and have been working hard and taking measures to address them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We all agree that what we should all do is to work towards a workplace culture where our older workers feel valued, and companies think about the needs of older workers when they put in place policies and practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: In fact, employers are recognising the benefits of having age-friendly and inclusive workplace practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: According to a 2016 survey by TAFEP, seven in 10 employers are willing to redesign job scopes to accommodate older workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: So, I am happy to say that the tripartite partners have developed a Tripartite Standard on Age-friendly Workplace Practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This Tripartite Standard will promote inclusive workplaces that meet the specific needs of older workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: More details will be shared later when the Standard is launched next month.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: As we continue to encourage inclusive behaviour, we will also take action against discriminatory practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: To counter any age discrimination in our workplaces, TAFEP looks into all age-discrimination complaints.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: MOM will not hesitate to take enforcement actions against errant employers who discriminate against older workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We strive to uplift their wages, enhance their employment conditions and improve their lives even as they work hard and make an honest living.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: First, through broad-based efforts, and second, through additional support for specific sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The WIS scheme is a key pillar of our support for low-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: As a permanent scheme, it helps low-wage workers build up their retirement savings and meet their daily needs as they work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Besides supplementing their income, Workfare Training Support (WTS) gives them opportunities to upskill and reskill to improve their employability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Zainal Sapari pointed out that some of our low-wage workers remain vulnerable and may face unfavourable working conditions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: MOM and CPF Board are aware of this.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We have stepped up public education and enforcement efforts through the WorkRight initiative.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: WorkRight ensures that low-wage workers are aware of and not denied their employment rights.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Today, eight in 10 employers inspected were found to have complied with the EA and CPF Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This is an increase from seven in 10 in 2012.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We take firm actions, including prosecution, against errant employers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Therefore, I urge Members to inform MOM if they come across workers who are denied their statutory employment rights.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: For specific sectors, we also take a more targeted approach.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: In particular, the tripartite partners have implemented mandatory PWM in the cleaning, security and landscaping sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Real wage growth of workers in PWM sectors has exceeded resident median income growth for the past five years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Workers in these sectors also now have clear progression pathways that commensurate with their skills and competencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: For the cleaning sector, the PWM was announced in 2012 and came into effect in 2014, and we have seen positive results over the years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: From 2011 to 2016, the real median gross wages of full-time resident cleaners grew by about 5.7% per annum.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We enhanced the Cleaning PWM in December 2016 to increase their wages further.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: And from 2020, cleaners will also enjoy a mandatory annual bonus equivalent to at least two weeks of monthly basic wages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Similarly, we have seen good progress for security officers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Since the PWM was launched in 2014 and implemented in 2016, the real median gross wage of full-time resident security guards grew by 6.4% per annum from 2011 to 2016.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The tripartite partners worked together to further enhance the security PWM in November 2017.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Over 34,000 resident security officers can now look forward to higher PWM basic wage increases each year of between 4.1% and to 5.7% for six years, from 1 January 2019.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: To transform the industry, the tripartite partners took a decisive step to improve the working hours of our security officers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: From 1 January 2021, MOM will no longer grant overtime exemption for the security industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This will reduce their current overtime hours from as high as 95 hours a month, to not more than the statutory limit of 72 hours.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: And to become more manpower-lean and productive, the industry is committed to adopt greater use of technology.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: And with these measures in place, workers will stand to benefit from having higher wages and shorter working hours.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This is something that we really want to do for our security officers to modernise the industry and also to professionalise their career.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: And we continue to work on improving their wages and working conditions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: With the cleaning and security PWM enhanced in 2016 and 2017 respectively, the tripartite partners will review and enhance the landscape PWM this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: More details will be announced by the Tripartite Cluster for Landscape Industry (TCL) after the tripartite negotiations have concluded.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The wages and employment conditions for low-wage workers across the board have improved over time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Over the past five years from 2012 to 2017, the real income growth at the 20th percentile (P20) of full-time employed citizens grew by 4.3% per annum, faster than at the median of 3.9% per annum.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: And for working hours, not only did their income increase, they also worked shorter hours.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Resident low-wage workers worked fewer hours per week, from 49 hours in 2012 to 46 hours in 2017.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: On job security, there was also greater job security for low-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: More workers were placed on permanent contracts and the number of casual on-call workers has decreased.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Even so, the work does not stop for us.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: In MOM, we will continue to work with the tripartite workers to support sustainable wage increases through PWM and raise employment standards through best sourcing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Given the good progress in the three PWM sectors, we want to see further adoption of PWM in other sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: PWM can benefit workers beyond low-wage workers, to other rank-and-file workers as well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: As a start, lift firms and unions are working with the Building and Construction Authority (BCA) to introduce a voluntary PWM for lift technicians.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This is especially useful, with a growing demand for lift technicians in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: More details will be announced by the industry when ready.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: MOM also stands ready to support the tripartite partners to develop and adopt PWM voluntarily for other sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Second, the Government will further safeguard the basic employment rights of outsourced workers in the cleaning, security and landscape sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Today, employment law criteria are already part of the professional accreditation and grading frameworks for the cleaning and security sectors respectively.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We will take a further step to introduce employment law criteria for the landscape sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: More details will be shared with the respective industries in the coming weeks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This means that companies in these three PWM sectors must treat their workers fairly in order to qualify for Government contracts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Through this measure, the Government is taking the lead.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The Labour Movement and the PWM tripartite committees led by Mr Zainal Sapari will urge more businesses to follow suit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Zainal Sapari is the champion for low-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: And I hope more businesses will heed the call and adopt similar best sourcing practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The tripartite partners will also continue to find ways to improve the employment conditions of workers in these PWM sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: To this end, the PWM tripartite committees should study further measures, such as Mr Zainal Sapari's proposal to mandate rest areas in these outsourced sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Zainal Sapari has also asked to compel employers to pay for outpatient treatment for low-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: However, our worry is that doing so may inadvertently affect the employability of workers with poorer health.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: So, this is the very group of vulnerable workers that the tripartite partners are trying to help.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We do not want to introduce something that may inadvertently create implications for them which will impact their employment opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Under our CPF system, employers are already required to contribute to their employees' MediSave.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: At the same time, the Government makes additional MediSave contribution to low-wage workers via schemes, such as WIS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: And we have our 3Ms, meaning MediSave, MediShield Life and MediFund, and other significant Government subsidies through schemes, such as the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS).

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: No Singaporean will be denied access to healthcare because of their inability to pay.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Zainal Sapari also called for mandatory AWS for low-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Under our existing Flexible and Performance-based wage systems, a worker's total annual wage package is made up of three components: monthly fixed component; monthly variable component and annual variable component where AWS is part of the annual variable component.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This design of monthly fixed, monthly variable and annual variable components varies widely across industries, companies and even occupations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: As such, the consensus of the tripartite partners is to give employers and unions the flexibility to negotiate their total annual wage package, including AWS, and not mandate the structure of the wage payments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Our initiatives will particularly help the group of older low-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: For example, they receive higher WIS payouts and benefit more from PWM.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Besides supporting older and low-wage workers, we should ensure that our workplaces are inclusive for all.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Not only should we make every worker a better worker, every job a better job, we should also do our best to make every workplace a better workplace.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
