text: A better and more inclusive workplace has no room for discrimination on account of gender, race or mental condition.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: And I thank Dr Intan, Mr Muhamad Faisal Manap, Assoc Prof Daniel Goh and Ms Tin Pei Ling for raising this point.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: To this end, all employers should embrace fair and merit-based employment, as stipulated in TGFEP.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: MOM will also take appropriate enforcement actions against employers found to have engaged in unfair employment practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: At the same time, we should make our workplace more accommodating towards persons with disabilities, as pointed out by Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: For example, the Open Door Programme (ODP) provides funding support to employers who hire persons with disabilities and redesign jobs for them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Melvin Yong, Mr Kok Heng Leun and Mr Louis Ng asked about protections and measures in place for our migrant workforce, including electronic payment of salary, employment contract and recruitment practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We are fully committed to protecting the well-being of our foreign workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: There are laws and policies for areas, including salary payment and local employment agency fees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: By law, foreign workers are to be issued the Key Employment Terms (KETs) within 14 days of arrival.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: To limit the financial burden on workers, local employment agencies are also prohibited from charging foreign workers recruitment fees more than one month of their salary per year of service.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We also ensure that foreign workers know their rights and responsibilities, and we assist them proactively when they need help.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We work with our partners, for example, the Migrant Workers Centre (MWC), to educate both workers and employers on the benefits of salary e-payment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: MWC also assists foreign workers with valid salary claims to seek employment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: As mentioned by Minister Lim Swee Say just now, this is the lowest rate recorded for the whole workforce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We are still lagging behind other countries with a workplace fatality rate of less than one.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Over the next 10 years, we must aspire to provide our workers with workplaces that are among the safest and healthiest in the world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: To do so, we need new breakthroughs in our strategy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We should chart out a comprehensive plan for WSH development over the next 10 years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Melvin Yong has given good ideas on how to improve our WSH programmes, such as near-miss reporting, WSH representatives in companies and many others.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The WSH2028 Committee will study all these suggestions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: While the WSH2028 Committee will formulate specific recommendations, I will now want to take this opportunity to sketch out broad areas that the Committee will look in.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: First, we will find ways to strengthen WSH ownership among companies and workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The Committee will study how we can influence everyone from C-suite executives to rank-and-file workers to being more committed to WSH.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Second, we should increase integration of workplace safety with workplace health as part of Total WSH.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Improving both workplace safety and workplace health is important because they reinforce each other.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We will study further ways to help companies detect and reduce both safety and health risks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Third, we need to deepen WSH capabilities of companies and workers, such as by raising the competencies of WSH professionals and improving the quality of WSH training providers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Fourth, we want to strengthen partnerships with different stakeholders to promote and reinforce positive WSH behaviour.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This includes having insurers price premiums more accurately based on claims history by companies, and technology companies providing solutions to detect risky work situations, and hospitals reintegrating injured workers as part of the Return-to-Work programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Lastly, the Committee will review the regulatory regime to ensure that it remains effective without excessive burden on compliant companies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The Committee will consider ideas, such as differentiating our enforcement approach based on firms’ or companies' past track records.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Through our tripartite efforts, we have made encouraging progress in these areas plus, as we always say, we are not satisfied with what the progress has been and will always look for new areas for improvements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: So, we will press on with our efforts to make Singapore a great workplace for our workers.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: I am glad to hear that MOM is looking for insurance for prolonged medical leave.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: They are, quite a lot of times, susceptible to injuries.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: So, I hope that this group can be included in it.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: There is a lot of possibility of casualties during the process.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: And I hope that it can also be included.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: For the third question, I wish to direct it to Minister of State Sam Tan.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: Previously, with regard to my questions, the Ministry had agreed to check on how the Koreans have been recruiting their foreign workers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to thank the Member for sharing his concerns about the dance community as well as the stage technicians.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will certainly be very keen to get in touch with the associations that they belong to and to explore ways in which we can promote the adoption of long medical leave insurance as a norm for their occupations.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Essentially, under the South Korean model, the Government becomes the Employment Agent for foreign workers.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Based on our experience, I do not think this will be practical for the Singapore situation.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: We have a far greater proportion of foreign workers in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: So, it is not feasible for the Government to be a surrogate employment agency for this big group of foreign workers.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: The South Korean model cannot guarantee that the source country where the foreign workers are imported from would take prudent measures or effective measures to protect the foreign workers from being exploited by the middlemen in the source country.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Under the South Korean system, the Government can do something to protect the interest of the foreign workers in South Korea, it does not have the jurisdictions to do something at the source country.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: We also work with many voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs) to help the foreign workers.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Lastly, we have also been actively engaging the foreign embassies where they have foreign workers working in Singapore to make sure, from time to time, that if there are issues concerning the well-being of their foreign workers, we can take up these issues with the foreign embassies.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: We ask them to pay attention on the treatment of their foreign workers within their own source country.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: All in all, we have studied this and, with due respect, it is something that it is still quite new in South Korea.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: We do not think that it would be practical for us to implement the same approach or same system in Singapore.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Chairman, the long-term unemployed includes those who are PMETs as well as rank-and-file.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For those persons who are helped, the help to them was real and not imagined.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As for profile, I am not sure exactly what Mr Low is seeking.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But if he could let me know, we will try and find out and share with him.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: We are, of course, concerned that many aspiring young people want to be freelancers, especially those who want to be private hire car drivers or taxi drivers.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: But moving forward, with the advent of things like autonomous vehicles, there may be a danger that some of them may enter into a career whereby they may be displaced.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: So, I would like to enquire if the career counsellors and coaches would be equipped to guide individuals who aspire to be freelancers to make an informed choice or to direct them towards employment that is of a permanent nature, such as an employee-employer relationship, other than the fact that they just make up their mind to probably enter into a lower entry barrier job of a freelancer.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Chairman, to Mr Ang's question, at present, if we look at the profile of the SEPs who took up self-employment work more recently, they are quite a mixed bag.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They include those that he highlighted, such as media freelancers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They also include people who have taken up work like private hire car driving.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The main thing is that it depends on whether they are doing it as their primary livelihood.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If they are doing it as a primary livelihood, then we are, of course, more interested in whether this is their preferred model of work.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, this is something that we can follow up on.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to respond to the comment made by hon Member Mr Low Thia Khiang.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: He mentioned just now that while we are looking after the well-being of foreign workers, we should also protect our local workers.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: He made a very important point here and I fully agree with him.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: In fact, our local workers are always close to our hearts.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: This is why we have very comprehensive legislation to protect the workers' rights.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: The Minister has mentioned earlier in his speech about making an amendment to the EA.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: We also have a slew of many other programmes like Adapt and Grow, PCP, CSP, WIS and all that.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: The sole purpose is to provide a wide range of programmes and assistance to help our local workers to adapt and grow and then also to develop, so that they will be able to secure better job security and employment prospects.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: I share totally Mr Low Thia Khiang's point that local workers are always the core interest of the Government.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Bearing in mind that while we look after the local workers, we should also treat our foreign workers fairly, so that there is this complementarity between the local and the foreign workers.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Otherwise, the ideal situation described by Minister Lim Swee Say of "two-thirds plus one-third, is greater than one" would not happen.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: If we treat our local workers better than foreign workers, then we will see the situation of "two-thirds plus one-third is less than one".

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: This is not the situation that we would like to see.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Mr Chairman, I have a question for Minister Lim Swee Say.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: The Minister of State Sam Tan correctly mentioned just now that MOM looks into cases of complaints of discrimination against, for example, older workers.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Mr Chairman, basically the disputes provided for under the EA are what MOM can handle.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: When ECT was set up, it was set up to handle only salary-related claims.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Even so, the tripartite partners decided that we will go on voluntary mediation for disputes which are not salary related.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In other words, we currently do not have the legal rights to mediate non-salary related claims, but we did it on the basis whereby we asked the employers/employees whether they are prepared to do so on a voluntary basis.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: With that in mind, we have decided why not take the next step to formalise it?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked whether some of these dispute resolutions would come under ECT.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For those wrongful dismissal disputes which are covered under EA, they will all be transferred to ECT.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In addition to that, because we have removed the salary ceiling, more people can now qualify for EA.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: As a result, more of them, next year, when we amend the Act, will be able to benefit from the one-stop service from ECT.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: But the Minister did share that some of the causes were relating to women stepping out of the workforce and then returning to the workforce.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: I do hope that MOM will work with the employers, if they are returning back to the workforce and they are doing the value of the job, and they do have the competencies for the job, they should not be penalised.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: They should be paid the same value of that job, and it should be performance-based rather than how long you have been in the job or whether you have taken time out of the workforce.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Member Ms Jessica Tan for giving me an opportunity to say a little bit more about how we look at the data.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I asked to look at the data within the public sector and it was quite interesting.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And as it turns out, the composition of the females and the males in the workforce also matters a great deal.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It turns out that the nature of the work performed by females in the public sector lend themselves to earning higher pay.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: What I would say is this: when we look at the gender pay gap, whether it is numbers compiled by ValuePenguin or whether it is even based on our comprehensive Labour Force Survey, we should not take it at face value.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The fact that more women might have exited the workforce and, as a result, in terms of cumulative length of service is perhaps not as high, that contributes to the gender pay gap.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Composition of the male workforce and the female workforce, and what kinds of work are being done, also matter.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If we dug deeper and looked at the gender pay gap within occupations, and then controlled for years of service, I half suspect that the gap is not going to look as high as it does.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But having said that, putting all of those things aside, it is still the right thing to do for us to enable as many women as possible to stay in the workforce, give them a chance to grow their careers, and not to have to choose between family and work.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is the right thing to do to enable them to fulfil all of their aspirations for work and family, and we will press on to do that.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Also, if we look at the whole slew of measures that can be taken, by far, the one that perhaps will make the most difference is the availability of FWAs because the reality of their lives are that, at home, there will still be responsibilities to be shared.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Even if they have a spouse, a partner, who is willing and able to chip in, very often, exigencies require them to take time out.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: How do we best enable persons with caregiving responsibilities, not just women, to remain active in the workforce?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That must be the thrust of our efforts.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to address this to the Second Minister.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: My question is similar to the hon Member Ms Jessica Tan; it is about the gender pay gap.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Because I shared the data in my speech earlier that, specifically, for those who are earning more than $11,000 a month, the number of male employees is twice that of female employees.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: If we can try and reduce that difference further in the senior management positions, that would be good.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Chairman, as I had explained, it is not entirely clear to me that there are, in fact, very significant gender pay gaps, after you have controlled for occupation and for years of service.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The best thing that we can do is go back to what will enable the women to make progress in their careers, which is not to exit, and the way in which to do it is to make FWAs available to them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For the other grades, as I had mentioned, sometimes, it has to do with the composition, what kinds of work they are doing.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: Does CTP apply to private and public sector and Government agencies, or is it only for the private sector?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: The second question is on workplace abuse and harassment.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: I just wish to know Second Minister Josephine Teo's take on what she feels about having a Tripartite Standard for managing workplace abuse and harassment rather than having it subsumed under the Grievance Handling or Grievance Management Tripartite Standard.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: This is to give more clarity to employers on how exactly to manage situations like that, rather than making it more a general statement under the Grievance Handling Tripartite Standard.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Mr Chairman, my answer is a quick one.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: That means, does it apply to the healthcare sector because it is like quasi-Government?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The healthcare sector, I think for the hospitals, you are not considered Government, right?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So long as you are a private sector organisation, you can apply.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Chairman, I have to address Ms Thanaletchimi's question.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I should say that these interventions can evolve over time.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will take the suggestion and we will look at it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I should also just supplement my reply to Dr Intan Mokhtar.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the private sector, it is very hard for the Government to intervene.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But I cannot imagine why in the private sector, the employers would not figure that they should reward according to talent.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If there are specific instances where someone has been discriminated against, I will be very interested to find out.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Second Minister for her responses to the Silver Support and CPF LIFE issues.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: Regarding the Second Minister's statement that Silver Support payouts using flat sizes is an uncomplicated way to measure household support, that is reasonable.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: The first question is I am wondering whether the cutting up of the payouts in the four tiers, 1- and 2-room flats is $750 and all the way to 5-room flats, it becomes $300.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: Is this too fine a banding and creating, therefore, a kind of complicated picture of household support that is much more complicated than what is on the ground?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: For one, 1-room and 2-room flats can be combined with 3-room flats.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: I think a lot of seniors who are caught up in that kind of situation where they need our support from Silver Support, living in those flats would be quite similar.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: The second question that I have is regarding the appeal process.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: The Second Minister said that it is an uncomplicated measure, yes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: But there could be complicated life situations that the seniors face due to support issues from household members.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: They might be living in 5-room flats and they might be making an appeal for eligibility.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: Could they also make an appeal in terms of the quantum?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As to the Member's other question about whether the flat type is cut too finely, well, service and conservancy charges are dependent on also that type of clustering.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, from that perspective, it has not been a difficulty.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: First with regard to my cut on Maternity Protection, can I ask whether Singapore will consider ratifying the ILO Convention on Maternity Protection?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Second, I might have missed the reply, but can MOM set up and maintain the public database for employers to voluntarily declare that they have written policies to manage workplace harassments or that they have implemented the Tripartite Advisory on Managing Workplace Harassment?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: The third question, to the Minister of State, is whether he can clarify why employers need to pay salaries of S Pass holders electronically but not for Work Permit holders.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I thought I should also respond to the Minister's shoelace story, just to share with Members of this House that if you do see a wild animal, it is best not to run.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Our laws provide sufficient protection against dismissal during pregnancy as well as Maternity Leave.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We do get referrals to look into cases and we will take the errant employers to task.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If Mr Louis Ng is aware of specific cases, we will certainly look into them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It does not always require for us to sign on to the ILO's Convention.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We are party to the declaration that the ILO has, and we have a very long-standing partnership with the ILO.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But all of the ILO Conventions are very binary in nature.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: When you sign on to one Convention, you must accept every single clause that is specified in the Convention.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The difficulty is that, sometimes, we are party to other treaties or agreements that would make it very difficult for us to adhere so strictly to all of the items specified.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Well, animal or no animal, some of us need to run.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Would the Member wish to withdraw his amendment?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: In closing, I thank my fellow Parliamentary colleagues who, together with me, filed 54 cuts and shared their thoughts, views, questions and suggestions.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: I believe it has thrown greater light on the challenges we face as a country and the right things we must do to better our work, workforce and workplaces amidst the backdrop of digitalisation, disruption and demographic changes.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: I would also want to thank Permanent Secretary Aubeck, Deputy Secretaries Augustine and Ping Soon and the MOM team, including the Statutory Boards, for their hard work behind the scenes.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: With that, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Order, I propose to take a break now.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 3.15 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 2.53 pm until 3.15 pm.
